title: Reliable, scalable animal-to-human organ transplantation

concept.text: Concept synthesis: This innovation would make organs from animals a reliable, reproducibly supplied option for human transplantation. Success would require an animal organ to perform its essential functions in a human recipient for years, with acceptable risks and a manageable treatment burden. The intended capability combines durable organ function with dependable production and clinical delivery; a single successful operation would demonstrate only part of it.

Scope synthesis: The central biomedical engineering challenge is compatibility between a living animal organ and the human body. Organ design or modification, immune management, physiological performance, and biological safety must work together. Gene editing is part of the pig-kidney approach described in the supplied research, but neither gene editing alone nor temporary graft function would establish reliable, scalable transplantation.

significance.text: Conditional impact synthesis: A safe, durable supply of animal organs could substantially expand transplantation through a biological source that can be bred and supplied reproducibly. The direct consequence would be an additional route to organ replacement. Shorter waits, broader eligibility, or earlier transplantation would be downstream possibilities if organ availability, patient outcomes, and clinical capacity supported them; these are potential consequences rather than demonstrated outcomes.

Impact limits synthesis: Reproducible production would not make organs unlimited or automatically accessible. Availability would still depend on breeding, screening, organ quality, surgery, immune management, pathogen surveillance, cost, and transplant infrastructure. Clinical value would also depend on how the risks and treatment burden compare with appropriate existing care. Animal organs and manufactured human organs address the same supply problem through different biological sources and production processes, so progress in one does not establish feasibility or readiness in the other.

missing_breakthrough.text: Research-goal synthesis: The missing capability is sustained compatibility across several interacting systems. The proposed organ must avoid acute and chronic rejection, harmful coagulation and inflammatory responses, and progressive tissue injury while reliably performing its physiological functions. Preventing an early destructive response would be insufficient if later injury gradually undermined the graft. The supplied material identifies these as barriers but does not provide inspectable scientific evidence establishing their relative importance or showing which interventions resolve them.

Engineering synthesis: Biological safety and supply reliability must be demonstrated alongside recipient compatibility. Concrete requirements include controlling the risk of animal-pathogen transmission, maintaining reproducible donor-animal and organ quality, and making screening and surveillance workable at clinical scale. Protection achieved through intensive treatment would also need evaluation for its infection risks and practical burden. These are proposed requirements derived from the concept, not capabilities established by the available source record.

current_state.text: The supplied research attributes a report titled “Porcine kidney xenotransplantation as a bridge to allotransplantation: a first-in-human study” to Leonardo V. Riella and colleagues, dated 3 September 2026, with DOI 10.1016/S0140-6736(26)01295-X. It describes a gene-edited pig kidney supporting one living recipient without dialysis for 271 days, followed by graft failure and removal and a subsequent human kidney transplant. It also attributes rejection and later microvascular injury to that course. These remain reported claims from the supplied research: the evidence review could not verify the article identity, clinical timeline, or pathology findings from the retained material.

The access limitation is substantive. According to the supplied review, the retained PubMed artifact contains only a cookie challenge, with no title, authors, abstract, or scientific results. The research's statements that an abstract was inspected and that the journal full text returned a 403 error are not corroborated by that artifact. Consequently, this record cannot establish whether the claimed report is a published clinical study, determine its publication status, or independently confirm its results. Missing accessible evidence does not establish that the report or its findings are false.

Interpretive synthesis: If verified, 271 days without dialysis in one recipient would demonstrate a meaningful period of kidney support and potential use as a bridge to human-organ transplantation. Graft failure and removal would limit that result's implications for durable replacement, while the single-recipient scope would leave reproducibility, recipient selection, longer-term outcomes, and scalable supply unresolved. No bounded search record was supplied to establish coverage through 1 November 2026; the artifact's retrieval on 11 November 2026 does not establish how complete the account of the field is.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical demonstration: Multicenter trials should show durable, organ-specific function and acceptable recipient survival, infection risk, and treatment burden relative to appropriate existing care. Protocols should specify follow-up periods, acceptance thresholds, recipient populations, and clinically meaningful outcomes in advance. For a capability intended to function for years, early postoperative success or temporary freedom from replacement therapy would be insufficient on its own. These are proposed evaluation principles, not established consensus standards.
completion_criteria.label: Multicenter trials demonstrate durable organ function and acceptable clinical outcomes

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and supply demonstration: Results should be repeatable across recipients, clinical teams, and independently produced donor organs. Evaluation should connect recipient outcomes to reproducible production, organ-quality assessment, pathogen screening, and ongoing surveillance. A convincing demonstration should also establish whether the surgery, immune-management regimen, monitoring, and supply process can be delivered with a practical treatment burden at the intended scale.
completion_criteria.label: Repeatable recipient outcomes with practical organ supply at intended scale

completion_criteria.text: Proposed boundaries of a completion claim: Evidence should state which animal source, organ type, recipient groups, treatment regimens, and duration of follow-up it covers. Successful kidney transplantation would not establish success for other organs, and a bridge-to-transplant application should be assessed separately from long-term replacement. Finite trials can establish demonstrated breadth and estimate observed risks; they cannot establish compatibility with every recipient or rule out every rare or delayed infection and graft failure.
completion_criteria.label: Completion claims state demonstrated transplantation scope and remaining risk limits

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: BME-01, “Manufacturing transplantable human organs on demand,” shares the goal of expanding organ supply, but proposes manufactured human organs rather than organs obtained from animals. BME-06, “Long-term banking of transplantable human organs,” addresses storage and availability of human organs. BME-11, “Controlled regeneration of complex organs in the adult body,” instead seeks restoration within the patient. BME-13, “Durable autonomous artificial-organ replacement,” pursues replacement through artificial systems. These are distinct routes to organ availability or restored function; success in animal-to-human transplantation would not complete any of them.

Roster-based synthesis: BME-08, “Reliable, antigen-specific immune tolerance,” overlaps directly with the immune-compatibility problem and could, conditionally, help reduce rejection or treatment burden. It would not by itself establish adequate organ physiology, control of coagulation and inflammation, pathogen safety, or reproducible supply. Conversely, a successful animal-organ transplant maintained with ongoing immune suppression would not necessarily demonstrate antigen-specific tolerance.

Roster-based synthesis: BME-02, “Programmable delivery of genetic therapies to most tissues,” concerns delivery of therapies within the body; it is distinct from modifying a donor animal or its organ. BME-10, “Validated patient-specific models for testing treatments before use,” and BME-18, “Long-lived continuous sensing of multiple clinically useful biomarkers,” could conditionally support treatment evaluation or monitoring, but neither would demonstrate transplant durability. These comparisons use the supplied roster titles; detailed specifications or evidence for the related entries were not provided.

change_log.change: Preserved BME-12 and its title while expanding the concept into a combined compatibility, durable-function, biological-safety, and supply capability.
change_log.reason: The innovation remains coherent despite the evidence gap, and both the research and review identify requirements beyond a single successful transplant.

change_log.change: Retained the reported 271-day result, clinical sequence, and injury findings with explicit attribution and uncertainty.
change_log.reason: The review found no inspectable scientific content verifying those details; that limitation warrants qualification rather than deletion or a finding that the claims are false.

change_log.change: Replaced the asserted successful abstract inspection and journal-access history with the review's documented limitation.
change_log.reason: The retained artifact contains a cookie challenge and does not corroborate either abstract inspection or a journal 403 response.

change_log.change: Separated conditional clinical significance from demonstrated outcomes and distinguished temporary bridging from durable replacement.
change_log.reason: Even if verified, a single recipient's period without dialysis would not establish years of reliable function, reproducibility, or scalable access.

change_log.change: Expanded completion proposals to include organ-specific follow-up, explicit acceptance thresholds, reproducibility, practical delivery, and bounded claims.
change_log.reason: The review identified missing protocol specificity; finite demonstrations cannot establish literal universality.

change_log.change: Used the supplied roster to explain relevant conceptual relationships while limiting comparisons to title-level scope.
change_log.reason: The final inputs provide BME-01's title and other roster entries, permitting a narrower comparison than the review could make without establishing their detailed specifications.

change_log.change: Distinguished evidence retrieval from coverage of the field through the requested as-of date.
change_log.reason: A retrieval timestamp does not substitute for a bounded search record or establish that the current-state account is comprehensive.

unresolved_issues: The identity, authorship, publication date, DOI, and publication status of the purported 2026 report require corroboration from scientific content.
The reported 271 days without dialysis, graft failure and removal, subsequent human kidney transplantation, and rejection and microvascular injury remain unverified.
The supplied material does not resolve whether an abstract was successfully inspected elsewhere or whether journal access returned a 403 error.
No bounded search record establishes coverage through 1 November 2026, so additional achievements or contrary findings may be absent.
Organ-specific follow-up periods, acceptable outcome thresholds, comparator care, recipient populations, and practical supply requirements remain to be defined.

Detailed comparisons with related concepts remain limited to the supplied roster titles. The review's recommendation to leave the BME-01 comparison wholly unassessed was narrowed because its title is now supplied; no detailed specification was inferred.
